Area of Study 1: Western Classical Tradition 1650-1910 — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 1: Western Classical Tradition 1650-1910 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: What is the name of the broken-chord accompaniment pattern common in Mozart's piano sonatas?
options: Alberti bass
Walking bass
Ground bass
Murky bass

mcqs.q: Which composer is most associated with the late-eighteenth-century Sturm und Drang style?
options: Mozart
Haydn
Clementi
Salieri

mcqs.q: What distinguishes Classical (1750-1820) from Baroque style?
options: Clearer melodic phrases, homophonic texture, balanced structures like sonata form.
Classical means any old serious music.
Music in 3/4 time.
Use of orchestra (Baroque had none).

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: Music in 3/4 time.
The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
It is always C major.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.
Music in 3/4 time.
Three sections: A, contrasting B, and a return to A (ABA).
Three different sections (ABC).
Classical means any old serious music.
